title: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
content:
In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.
OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.
Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.)
Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree. (OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in-house search index, although there is still some speculation that it routes some queries through Google.)
The news comes amid an ongoing search engine shake-up, as Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third-party sites and invests heavily in AI tools — not just AI Overview but also additional generative AI capabilities, including personalized search results with visualizations and charts. But as search queries increasingly route through OpenAI and other AI labs’ services, other companies are investing in the same types of AI-focused search experience, even if they call it something else: for OpenAI, it’s “Intelligent UI,” or creating a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response. “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” Fry said.
Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year. OpenAI has defended its ads in the past, and Fry told reporters they hadn’t produced a lasting backlash. “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” he said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.”
OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before.
“Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.

report.summary: OpenAI says ChatGPT search query volume now equals 20% of Google's, signaling AI chatbots are becoming a real alternative to traditional search.
report.background: Search is one of the internet’s most valuable gateways, historically dominated by Google and monetized through ads. Microsoft’s Bing spent more than a decade trying to challenge Google but held only about 3% market share by 2023, according to Satya Nadella’s testimony in Google’s antitrust trial. That trial also framed AI as a potential disruptor, with Google warning that ChatGPT could seriously compete. Since then, Google has leaned into AI Overviews and generative features while reducing conventional referrals to third-party sites. OpenAI, meanwhile, is building search directly into ChatGPT and positioning it as part of a broader “Intelligent UI” strategy, with ads and a possible IPO adding commercial pressure.
key_points: OpenAI’s metric: ChatGPT search queries now equal 20% of Google’s volume. OpenAI defines a search as a query that triggers a web search, excluding simple definitions or how-to answers. That makes the comparison narrower than all Google searches, and OpenAI did not disclose its source for Google’s volume.

The 20% figure is far ahead of Bing’s roughly 3% share after a decade of trying, showing AI chat can change search habits faster than conventional search engines. Still, one-fifth is not dominance, and OpenAI likely relies partly on Bing and its own index.

Google is responding by cutting conventional referrals to publishers and pushing AI Overviews plus generative, personalized results with charts and visualizations. At the same time, rivals are building AI-native search experiences, which OpenAI calls “Intelligent UI”—interactive, visual answers inside a chat canvas.

OpenAI sees ads as a path to profitability, especially ahead of a potential IPO. It has begun showing sponsored product images in ChatGPT, not just names and links. OpenAI says ads have not hurt usage or product quality, and Fry suggests the company could do more with ads.
report.impact: For the AI industry, OpenAI’s claim reframes competition around answer engines rather than ten blue links. If ChatGPT sustains 20% of Google’s search volume, ad budgets, publisher traffic, and search infrastructure could shift toward AI interfaces. Developers should expect more demand for retrieval, citation, ranking, and ad-integration tooling, plus APIs that blend chat with live web data. Regular users may get faster, more conversational answers, but also fewer outbound clicks to sources and more sponsored results inside AI responses. The bigger risk is concentration: a few AI platforms could mediate discovery, shaping what people find and which publishers survive. That makes trust, attribution, and transparency central product issues.
report.tools: To follow the shift, watch ChatGPT Search, Google AI Overviews, Microsoft Copilot/Bing, and Perplexity. For hands-on testing, try SearXNG, a privacy-focused open-source metasearch engine, and Perplexica, an open-source AI search interface that combines language models with web retrieval. Developers can also explore Open WebUI with search integrations, LangChain retrieval tools, and citation/ranking APIs to prototype answer-engine experiences.
